messages:
maya: RFC follow-up — proposing a 'dual-image swap' pattern for on‑prem / air-gapped upgrades. Goal: atomic switch, minimal live rewrite, fast rollback, and safe verification in strict environments. Thoughts? :thinking:

sam: high level is clear. how do we avoid doubling disk usage for big model artifacts? worst-case customers won't have spare TBs.

jordan: we use an overlay + layered artifact approach. copy only metadata and changed layers; models as immutable layer blobs. practically: write new layers into /opt/releases/<ts>/layers/, then prepare an overlay mount rather than copying whole FS. that avoids full dupes for unchanged files.

liam: also add a streaming chunker to move large blobs off USB to local registry appliance. appliance verifies signature + hashes then exposes a local OCI-like registry. that avoids rewriting across every node.

maya: sketch of lifecycle (very short):

1) controller pushes signed release bundle (signed-manifest + layer blobs) to local relay appliance (airgapped transfer).
2) appliance verifies signatures, exposes bundle to cluster nodes via local registry or temp NFS.
3) node fetches new layers into /opt/releases/<ts>/layers/ (chunked, resumable).
4) node mounts overlay: lower=previous, upper=/opt/releases/<ts>/upper, work=/opt/releases/<ts>/work then does service swap by updating symlink /opt/current -> /opt/releases/<ts>/root and sending SIGHUP or use rolling restart.

example commands (illustrative):

```bash
mkdir -p /opt/releases/1865000010/{layers,upper,work,root}
# fetch layers into layers/ (resumable chunker)
# prepare overlay mount for runtime to probe new FS before swap
mount -t overlay overlay -o lowerdir=/opt/current,upperdir=/opt/releases/1865000010/upper,workdir=/opt/releases/1865000010/work /opt/releases/1865000010/root
# smoke tests: /opt/releases/1865000010/root/bin/serve --smoke
ln -sfn /opt/releases/1865000010/root /opt/current_new_tmp
# controlled swap (atomic symlink swap)
ln -sfn /opt/releases/1865000010/root /opt/current
# post-swap signal
systemctl restart redwood-runtime.service
```

jordan: key safety nets: signature verification first, then smoke tests against the mounted overlay before touching live symlink. If smoke tests fail, unmount + garbage collect incomplete release.

sam: rollback semantics? if new release breaks, how do we ensure instant revert without lengthy data migration?

maya: dual-image helps — keep previous release intact and preserve its state dirs. for quick rollback we swap symlink back to previous release and restart. to avoid incompatible on-disk state we negotiate migration via a version handshake: runtime exposes `POST /_upgrade_probe` with fields `expected_migration=v2` and `dry_run=true`. new runtime must support fallback.

liam: service-level migration: split migrations into idempotent, small steps. store migration state in durable `upgrade-state.json` per node so rollback can detect partially-applied migrations and auto-reverse safe ops.

jordan: also recommend runtime feature gating: new runtime advertises supported features in its health endpoint. controller will only flip traffic to nodes that report compatible feature set.

maya: resource concerns: GC policy must be conservative. keep last N releases (N=2 by default) and background-evict older ones only when disk > threshold. share layers between releases to save space.

sam: how do we handle large model checkpoint transformations (quantize, reformat) that are not reversible?

liam: approach: do heavy, irreversible transformations off-node on the appliance and publish transformed read-only blobs. nodes only download final blob. keep original blobs in archival media if customer wants rollback to older model format (expensive, but explicit).

devops-bot: upgrade-scan 1865000010 verification: signatures OK, smoke-tests passed on canary nodes (canary=3), disk usage delta within thresholds. :white_check_mark:

maya: good. next steps: update RFC with overlay mount details, handshake API (`/_upgrade_probe`), and appliance transfer protocol. I'll file a follow-up doc with sequence diagrams and a minimal state machine. link: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/dual-image-swap (placeholder).

jordan: :thumbsup: one nit — ensure we have metrics: `upgrade.swap.duration`, `upgrade.fetch.retries`, `upgrade.gc.age`. we need alert thresholds before GC.

sam: also add a forced-clean mode for constrained nodes where we avoid keeping previous image (explicit opt-in). must warn customers about rollback limitations.

maya: agreed. I'll add those to the RFC and call a quick design review next Tue. thanks everyone. :raised_hands:
